question:
In the given figure, angle ABC = 120circ, angle EDC = 120circ. AB is parallel to DE. What is the value (in degrees) of angle BCD?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64d1e0670616cee7c21beaba8845d5191c914c98491022c4dd87af0902a868ba.png]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Draw a line parallel to **AB** passing through point **C**.

Angle between **BC** and the parallel line = 180° − 120° = 60° (**Consecutive Interior Angles**).

Angle between **CD** and the parallel line = 180° − 120° = 60° (**Consecutive Interior Angles**).

The total angle at point **C** on a straight line is 180°.

∠BCD = 180° − (60° + 60°) = 60°.

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

∠ABC = 120°

∠EDC = 120°

**AB** ∥ **DE**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2ff6dc4b6e9fd7e85b046bc3e7af28d2fc7190f4feb38bc2c53528f0c6df1c3c.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculation:**

⇒ Let us draw a line **PCQ** passing through **C** such that **PQ** ∥ **AB** ∥ **DE**.

⇒ Since **AB** ∥ **PQ**, then ∠ABC + ∠BCP = 180° (Sum of **consecutive interior angles**).

⇒ 120° + ∠BCP = 180°

⇒ ∠BCP = 180° − 120° = 60°

⇒ Since **DE** ∥ **PQ**, then ∠EDC + ∠DCQ = 180° (Sum of **consecutive interior angles**).

⇒ 120° + ∠DCQ = 180°

⇒ ∠DCQ = 180° − 120° = 60°

⇒ Now, **PCQ** is a straight line, so ∠BCP + ∠BCD + ∠DCQ = 180°.

⇒ 60° + ∠BCD + 60° = 180°

⇒ ∠BCD + 120° = 180°

⇒ ∠BCD = 180° − 120° = 60°

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Consecutive Interior Angles

When two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal, the pairs of angles on the same side of the transversal inside the parallel lines are supplementary (Sum = 180°).

Alternate Interior Angles

Angles located between parallel lines and on opposite sides of the transversal are equal (∠1 = ∠2).

Angle on a Straight Line

The sum of all angles formed at a point on one side of a straight line is always 180°.
